title: Ahab's selective human agency
agencyClaim: Ahab exercises responsible human agency by preferring favorable counsel and resisting adverse prophecy.
manifestations: favorable prophecy is desired while Micaiah's adverse speech is rejected
assumptions: the narrative presents Ahab's speech as meaningful for interpreting his agency
falsifiers: a reading that shows Ahab's stated preference is incidental rather than interpretively significant

title: Royal court consultation system
agencyClaim: The courtly counsel system contributes to the decision environment by organizing prophetic speech around royal desire and public deliberation.
manifestations: prophetic messages are performed in a royal setting before a military decision
assumptions: the narrative's court setting is relevant to the production and reception of prophecy
falsifiers: evidence that the court setting has no interpretive role beyond incidental location

title: Prophetic symbolic mediation
agencyClaim: Competing prophetic speech mediates the meaning of the royal decision by staging favorable authorization and adverse warning.
manifestations: the decision is interpreted through rival prophetic messages
assumptions: prophetic speech functions as more than background information in the narrative
falsifiers: a stronger reading that the narrative is uninterested in prophetic mediation as a distinct level

title: Lying spirit mediated through prophets
agencyClaim: The lying spirit is proposed by the text as a nonhuman spiritual agent whose deceptive agency is mediated through prophetic speech.
manifestations: deception is linked to a spirit's proposed role in the mouths of prophets
assumptions: the council vision is relevant to agency attribution rather than merely decorative narration
a narrated spirit can be considered as a proposed nonhuman spiritual agent within a defined biblical-theological frame
falsifiers: a theological or literary reading that prohibits treating the spirit as a distinct agent even within the narrative world
evidence that the passage is being used to make claims outside its textual scope without warrant
notes: Human review remains required before any spiritual attribution is approved or generalized.

title: Divine judicial agency in the council scene
agencyClaim: The narrative presents YHWH's judicial agency as governing the council scene while remaining distinguishable from the spirit's proposed mediation and Ahab's responsibility.
manifestations: the council vision frames the proposed deception within divine judgment
assumptions: the narrative's depiction of YHWH is germane to theological agency attribution
divine permission and creaturely agency should not be collapsed
falsifiers: a theological reading that treats the council scene as non-attributive imagery only
an interpretation that collapses divine agency into the spirit's agency or removes Ahab's responsibility
notes: This hypothesis is textual-theological and does not authorize automated theological adjudication.
